summary: Rest day in Moab after a 100-mile day with six flats. The team cooled off in the Colorado River, got frozen yogurt, toured Arches, and hiked to Delicate Arch.
planning_notes: Moab: the Colorado River is a cool-off option but the current is strong. The Delicate Arch hike is about 3 miles with rocky scrambles and not much elevation.

summary: Ran errands in Moab (bike shop, supplies, library), then rode an evening 34-mile route to Wingate Campground and raced sunset without a front light.
slept_at: Wingate Campground, Dead Horse State Park, UT
contacts: Rim Cyclery, Moab UT (checked bikes, replaced chains, sold water bottle cages and spare tubes)
planning_notes: Moab: Rim Cyclery checks bikes and sells water bottles, cages and spare tubes. Stock up on spare tubes before the desert.
Interstate shoulders were wide and legal on the sections they rode, but debris caused about 10x more flats. Carry tubes.
The evening ride from Moab into Dead Horse State Park ends in dusk. Bring a front light; one rider forgot theirs and barely made it before dark.

summary: Rode US-91 and I-70 across high desert to Green River, stopping at a novelty 'AREA STUPID' gas station and racing last year's team's Strava times on a tailwind downhill.
slept_at: Green River State Park Campground, UT
planning_notes: Green River State Park Campground has eight showers, which the team called glamping.
The Green River library had space for work in the evening, and the team used it.

summary: Flats before leaving camp, then the support van got stuck on rough gravel and missed the first water stop, so riders collected 16 water bottles from strangers on the highway. Rode about 100 miles through Hanksville to Capitol Reef and swam in the Fremont River, which later tested above recommended E. coli levels.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground (name not stated)
contacts: Rebecca's parents (phone help that got the support van moving again; location not stated)
planning_notes: Support van route: a Google Maps route set to avoid interstates led onto rough gravel and boulders in the Utah desert. The van got stuck and missed the first water stop. Check the support vehicle's road surface before going off interstates.
Water: on this 100-mile desert day the team had no support at the first water stop and relied on strangers. Carry extra water.
Fremont River near Capitol Reef: the team swam, and later learned E. coli was above recommended levels. Skip swimming there.

summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef: a grocery run to a town about 30 minutes away, a cafe and ice cream stop in Torrey, laundry and route planning, and a late hike in which three riders took the Rim Overlook trail by mistake instead of Hickman Bridge.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground (name not stated)
planning_notes: Hickman Bridge trail (1.8 miles round trip): the fork is easy to misread, and the Rim Overlook trail goes the opposite way.
Grocery run: the nearest town is about 30 minutes from Capitol Reef. Restock there before going back into the park.
Torrey's general store had space to work, with wifi, and the nearby cafe roasts its beans in-house.

summary: A long day (78 miles, 7,365 ft) through a national forest, a narrow ridge road, and desert on Utah Scenic Byway 12. Cleo crashed at speed on a steep descent where she had skipped braking, broke her arm, and was out at least four weeks. This was the team's first accident.
planning_notes: Utah Scenic Byway 12: climbs of 10-13% grade and a 14% four-mile descent. A narrow ridge road has cliffs on both sides.
Steep descents: one rider skipped brakes on downhills, skidded off the road at speed, and broke an arm. Control speed on steep descents.
Kiva Koffeehouse, in the canyon on Byway 12: raspberry lemonade, pastries, and canyon views. Previous Spokes teams recommended it.
Every recent Spokes team has had at least one injury. The crash required a hospital visit (location not stated).

summary: An easy 47-mile ride to Bryce Canyon, with a cow race and a town misspelling of Hank's name. The afternoon was a hike among the hoodoos, and the evening was dinner at Bryce Canyon Lodge and stargazing with a family member.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon campground (name not stated; uncle Paul's campsite nearby)
contacts: Uncle Paul (family member who took the team to dinner at Bryce Canyon Lodge)
planning_notes: Bryce Canyon Lodge served the team a sit-down dinner after the ride.
The trail out of Bryce's canyon has steep switchbacks. The team sprinted them and was exhausted afterward.

summary: A timestamped log of an 80-mile ride from Bryce to Zion, with headwinds on UT-12. At lunch Cleo decided to go home. In Zion the bikes could not go through the Mt. Carmel Tunnel, so Jess shuttled the riders through by van. The team got Angel's Landing permits.
slept_at: Zion National Park campsite (Watchman Campground, per the following day's post)
planning_notes: Mt. Carmel Tunnel (Zion's east entrance): bikes are not allowed, and there is no room to pass. Plan for a van shuttle through the tunnel.
Angel's Landing permits are awarded by lottery. The decision letter comes ahead of the hike, so check the timing.

summary: Rest day in Bryce. Cleo had fractured her right elbow two days earlier (four-week estimate, no biking), and she weighed staying as a passenger against flying home to France. The team hiked the hoodoos and ate ice cream.
slept_at: Bryce Canyon campground (name not stated)
planning_notes: Bryce Canyon gets surprisingly cold on summer nights. Bring warm layers for camping.

summary: Hiked Angel's Landing on a lottery permit. Then the team had a Thai dinner and a farewell dance for Cleo, who left the team the next morning.
slept_at: Zion campground (Watchman Campground, per the following day's post)
planning_notes: Angel's Landing: take the shuttle to the trailhead. Permits are checked at Scout Lookout. The last 0.5 miles are a ridge with chains to hold, and drop-offs on both sides. Expect a slow pace.

summary: Sent Cleo off toward St. George for her bus and plane home. Then hiked The Narrows of the Virgin River from the Zion bus stop, and biked to a Motel 6 in Hurricane with exhausted legs.
slept_at: Motel 6, Hurricane, UT
planning_notes: Zion Outfitter, in the town near the park, rents boots, hiking poles, and waterproof backpacks for The Narrows. Return the gear there after the hike.
The Narrows: ride the park bus to the drop-off, then walk about 1 mile to the official start. Expect deep, cold crossings and crowds later in the day.
Biking about 20 miles after two hard hiking days felt worse than a century. Plan light after heavy hikes.

summary: A long, dull 100-mile day from Hurricane to Milford. The route went about 90 miles northeast, away from the West Coast. Riders had flats, a first lunch of Cedar City fast food, a drafting crash, and a team cheesesteak dinner after a night at a church.
slept_at: Mountain View Baptist Fellowship, Milford, UT (church)
contacts: Mountain View Baptist Fellowship, Milford UT (overnight stay)
planning_notes: Route check: this day's route went 90-some miles northeast before heading west. Verify the direction of long route segments before leaving.
Cedar City, UT has McDonald's, Dairy Queen, Culver's and gas stations. It is a rare resupply on this stretch.
Drafting: riding too close behind another rider caused a crash. Keep a safe gap, because the rider in back is the one who gets hurt.

summary: A hot, empty US-50 ride from Milford into Nevada, with a shoulder lunch and no services. The team crossed into Pacific Time and posed at the Nevada sign. In Baker, pop. 21, they had ice cream and dinner, then a night festival with live music at the general store.
slept_at: RV site in Baker, NV (name not stated)
planning_notes: US-50 in Nevada has long stretches with no services. Carry water and food, because the team ate lunch on the shoulder.
Baker, NV has no grocery store. Bring dinner supplies from the last town.
Sugar, Salt & Malt in Baker serves housemade sorbet and ice cream sandwiches and is a strong meal stop.
The Nevada state line sign has Spokes stickers from past teams. The general store sells kombucha.

summary: The Nevada mountain ranges start: about 4,300 ft of climbing on a 'short' 61-mile day to Ely. Barbed wire gashed a rider's hand at the campground, lunch slid to 3 pm, and the team recovered poolside at a motel in Ely.
slept_at: Motel in Ely, NV (name not stated; has a pool)
planning_notes: Barbed wire by the Baker campground: check the tent site for fencing before setting up.
Nevada ranges between Baker and Ely add up to about 5,400 ft of climbing on 61 miles. Count elevation as well as distance.

summary: A sticker-collection recap of the whole trip. The day itself was 50 miles of Nevada wasteland to a shoulder lunch, then 30 more miles to a camp at the county fairground in Eureka. Stops covered include Breaks Interstate Park hammocks, the Osawatomie, KS host, Tallgrass headwinds, JJ Mercantile water on UT-128, and the Baker night market.
slept_at: County fairground, Eureka, NV
contacts: Jeff and Sarah, Osawatomie, KS (hosted the team; run a bike shop from their home)
planning_notes: Osawatomie, KS is the start of the 118-mile Flint Hills Trail.
Tallgrass Prairie visitor center (KS): 15 miles of very strong headwinds before it. The visitor center was a shelter stop.
JJ Mercantile on UT-128 was the only water for about 20 miles in either direction. The power went out while a rider was filling a bottle.
Mammoth Cave (KY): squirrels opened bike bags. Secure food and bags against squirrels, and note that squirrels overran a Utah campsite so badly that rangers checked on the team.

summary: Cleo's non-biking day in Porto, Portugal with her family. The post also includes riders' quotes about their Eureka to Austin, Nevada ride (67.7 mi, 2,943 ft).
planning_notes: Eureka to Austin, NV on US-50: long stretches broken by small mountain ranges. Riders reported shoulder lunches, loud military aircraft overhead, and downhills after climbs as the best motivation.

summary: The longest ride of the trip, 112 miles on the Loneliest Road in America (US-50), in 99°F heat and headwinds. The rider went solo until the Middlegate stop at mile 64, then pushed on alone to the Fallon Youth Club for dinner with the host.
slept_at: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon, NV
learning_festival: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon NV, hosted by Shannon. Activities are described in the following day's post.
contacts: Shannon, Fallon Youth Club (fed the team a warm dinner)
planning_notes: US-50, Austin to Fallon: 16 mountain ranges across the Great Basin stretch. All the climbing is in the first half. The last 20 miles are flat, but with headwinds.
Middlegate, NV (pop. 17): a bar with ice water and a rest stop at mile 64. There are no services for long stretches before it.
Heat: the temperature reached 99°F in the afternoon. Start early and carry extra water.
A subpar bike repair left a rider's bike unusable. Ask the mechanic to test-ride the bike and listen for the sounds you're concerned about.
Knee pain: dropping a gear and pedaling faster reduced strain on one rider's knee.

summary: A learning festival day at the Fallon Youth Club: Strawberry DNA extraction, a Physics of Sound speaker workshop, and catch-and-run with students. The team also found out about US-50 road work between Fallon and Silver Springs. The detour decision was postponed to the morning.
slept_at: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon, NV
learning_festival: Fallon Youth Club: Strawberry DNA and Physics of Sound workshops with students, cafeteria bottle flipping. Hosted by Shannon.
contacts: Shannon, Fallon Youth Club (hosted the team, cooked dinner, did laundry, shared the club's history)
planning_notes: Strawberry DNA: dish soap breaks down membranes, salt neutralizes DNA charge so strands stick together, and rubbing alcohol makes DNA visible. Works well with students.

Physics of Sound speaker kit: 3D-printed base, permanent magnet, copper wire wrapped on a paper cylinder, cardstock, and super glue. Have adults do the gluing so no one glues their fingers. Speakers sound louder when taped to a metal trash can.

US-50 road work between Fallon and Silver Springs: one-way sections with pilot cars, 25 mph limits, delays up to 30 minutes, and sections up to 5 miles. The Nevada DOT phone line had closed by the time the team learned of it, so call when it opens at 8 am.
Detour: US-50 Alt to Fernley adds about 15 miles and 500 ft of climbing. Few paved alternate roads exist in this part of Nevada.

summary: Took the 15-mile detour to avoid Nevada road work, then climbed the Carson Range from about 4,700 to over 7,100 ft. The team descended into California on a shoulderless road. Amulya's dead backlight meant a van pickup after dark.
slept_at: Resort in South Lake Tahoe (booked by Lake Tahoe STEM Academy)
contacts: Lake Tahoe STEM Academy (booked the team's resort for the night)
planning_notes: US-50 Carson Range climb toward Lake Tahoe: about 4,700 to 7,100 ft in a couple of miles with a relentless grade. Wildfire smoke hid the lake.
US-50 descent into South Lake Tahoe has no shoulder. A rider with a dead backlight needed a van pickup after dark. Carry working lights.
The Fernley reroute (US-50 Alt) goes through Fernley. The state capitol and monuments in Carson City are a stop along the way.
The California state line on US-50 has only a small green road sign, which is easy to miss.

summary: The day after a 15-mile pickup from a dark, shoulderless road. The team rode to the Lake Tahoe STEM Academy at the Boys & Girls Club. The writer taught fourth graders Strawberry DNA, saw a black bear near the field, and watched high school robotics teams test boats.
slept_at: Campsite near Lake Tahoe (name not stated; had cell service)
learning_festival: Lake Tahoe STEM Academy at the Boys & Girls Club, South Lake Tahoe: Strawberry DNA with fourth graders, and a visit to high school robotics teams testing boats and a paddleboard motor. Run with founder David.
contacts: David, founder of Lake Tahoe STEM Academy (MIT alum), Lake Tahoe Boys & Girls Club
planning_notes: Lake Tahoe Boys & Girls Club: a small group of students made it easy to learn names and run Strawberry DNA well.
A black bear was seen near the Boys & Girls Club field. Keep food and bags secured in the area.
When a day runs past dusk, call for a pickup instead of riding shoulderless roads in the dark.

summary: A rest day in South Lake Tahoe: cafe-hopping and work, a call with Cleo, then a lake boat outing and dinner hosted by Marina and Rafael. Hank and JD shipped the learning festival materials back to Boston.
slept_at: Campsite in South Lake Tahoe (name not stated)
contacts: Marina and Rafael, Lake Tahoe (Hank's aunt's friends; hosted a boat outing and dinner at their lakeside condo)
planning_notes: Learning festival materials were shipped from South Lake Tahoe back to Boston. Plan this before the final leg.
Keys Cafe and Cuppa Tahoe in South Lake Tahoe were good places for high-speed wifi and work.

summary: A rest day in Lake Tahoe. Amulya fell off a curb while biking to the resort, hit her head and shoulders, and was treated at a hospital for a minor concussion. The hospital said she could still bike. The team had a lackluster beach visit and cooked congee.
planning_notes: California prices in Tahoe: about $6 per gallon of gas and $6 per ice cream scoop.
A Safeway in the Lake Tahoe area gives out free bread after 5 pm.
A curb fall on the way to a resort lobby caused a minor concussion. Ride carefully on curbs and in parking lots.

summary: A 90-mile day over Carson Pass, with a 1,000-ft climb at about 8% and then a long downhill through the Caldor Fire burn area. The team stopped at the Carson Pass visitor center for free watermelon and ate lunch by an alpine lake. They reached a church host in Placerville after getting lost looking for it.
slept_at: Church in Placerville, CA (name not stated)
contacts: Larry, volunteer at the Carson Pass visitor center (gave the team free watermelon)
planning_notes: After leaving South Lake Tahoe: a 1,000+ ft climb at about 8% average on a narrow road that passes through a campground. Expect slow cars.
Caldor Fire burn area (2021): long stretches of burned trees. Campsites on this route had fire bans.
Carson Pass visitor center: the volunteer offers free watermelon. The team spent about 30 minutes there.
Church host in Placerville: navigation is tricky to find the church. Get directions in advance.

summary: Cleo's post covers her family's Portugal trip. Varsha's riders' post covers a flat ride from Placerville to Sacramento along the American River trail, a French bread lunch, Salt and Straw ice cream, dinner with host Bob, and a Chinese buffet.
slept_at: Host Bob's home, Sacramento, CA (name not stated)
contacts: Bob, Sacramento, CA (host for the night; long-time bike tourer and racer with a garage of bike gear)
planning_notes: American River bike trail (Sacramento): flat, scenic, and busy with other riders. One trail section had an 18% grade, the team's steepest of the summer.
French bread sandwiches make a good calorie-dense lunch, and the team found them too late in the trip. A park with palm trees near downtown Sacramento was a lunch stop.
Salt and Straw (Sacramento) is a unique-flavor ice cream stop.

summary: Sacramento to Benicia (72 miles). A non-hitch bike rack fell off the minivan on a speed bump and dragged two bikes. The rack was reattached and the bikes went to a shop. The riders also dealt with detours and flats. The rest of the post is a 28-item to-do list by state.
planning_notes: Support van bike rack: the minivan has no hitch, so the non-hitch rack fell off over a speed bump and dragged bikes. A hitch-mounted rack is a safer choice for a long trip.
A Sacramento-area bike shop replaced one wheel and repaired a derailleur. It could not fix a shredded tire and sanded rims on another bike, and ran out of time.
Kentucky: aggressive dogs. Tactics that worked were sprinting, walking the bike, and barking back.
Illinois: a campsite next to Rend Lake, with a warm swim.
Colorado: the CR 742 descent from the Continental Divide, near Gunnison, was the team's favorite scenery.
A detour near a chemical plant led police to be called on a rider. Be cautious near industrial sites.
